14                PASTOR MILLER:   Let us take a 

15   moment to silently center ourselves, or to offer 

16   our own meditations, or to join me in prayer.

17                Oh, Holy One, source of all that 

18   is, we come ready to do the holy work -- yes, 

19   the holy work -- of ordering this society and 

20   the lives of Your people entrusted to our care 

21   in this State of New York in which You've placed 

22   us.

23                We're thankful for the opportunity 

24   to work with our colleagues surrounding us in a 

25   state full of wonder and beauty -- towering 


                                                                2274

 1   buildings, soaring mountains, seashores, 

 2   lakeshores, rivers and swamps.  

 3                Some of us come alert, energetic 

 4   and hopeful, others with varying degrees of 

 5   fatigue, cynicism or anxiety.  But all of us 

 6   come aware that we work, deliberate, and 

 7   decide -- not to get our own way or to exert our 

 8   own will, or even necessarily the wills of our 

 9   constituents, but on behalf of the common good.  

10                We come here with enough 

11   self-awareness to know that to a large extent, 

12   those of us gathered here are a privileged 

13   people.  We are a gathering of the suits, the 

14   men and the women with good education and the 

15   best connections, people of power who know how 

16   to have our voices heard.  

17                And so we come bearing a special 

18   responsibility, and require thus Your special 

19   guidance.  We need a special measure of 

20   self-awareness and a spirit of generosity and 

21   goodheartedness, so that we can check our power 

22   and represent well those who are absent from 

23   this gathering -- the poor, the elderly, the 

24   unemployed and underemployed, minorities under 

25   threat, prisoners who live at the edge of their 


                                                                2275

 1   constitutional rights, and the many who do not 

 2   participate in our privilege.

 3                It's easy to forget that there are 

 4   those around us who live lives of deficit, cut 

 5   off from power and denied access to the gains we 

 6   enjoy.  And so, O God, help us to yield our 

 7   wills to Yours.  Help us to bring order amidst 

 8   our disorder.  Help us to see the larger 

 9   picture, to dream greater dreams, to imagine a 

10   brighter future, because we cannot realize what 

11   we cannot imagine.  

12                Help us to discern priorities 

13   divested from our perch of privilege and to look 

14   beyond our own perceived sense of scarcity to 

15   the abundance of resources entrusted to us.  

16                O God, help us to govern and to 

17   legislate for the sake of the lives of others 

18   until all people in this state can live lives of 

19   opportunity, lives healthy and whole.

20                Amen.
